p: Physically-grounded depth grade for astrophotographs using Gaia distances. Defaults to the offline local Gaia DR3 database (the one PixInsight uses for plate-solving; no network use); an online option queries the ESA Gaia archive over HTTPS for Bailer-Jones distances. Linux x64 only: needs the "Gaia Depth Grade sidecar" package from this repository, and StarXTerminator. Documentation, including network use, the programs it runs and the files it writes: doc/scripts/GaiaDepthGrade/GaiaDepthGrade.html.

Enlarged (near) stars wear a star-shine halo whose radial shape is stacked from the frame's own bright, unsaturated, isolated stars and tinted to each star's own colour; frames with too few clean reference stars fall back to a Moffat profile, with a warning. Optional nebula depth (off by default) grades the starless layer too: dark dust and globules come forward and the diffuse glow recedes, with the overall strength calibrated by the Gaia matched-star distance spread, and Nebula depth / atmospheric / structure sliders.

The sidecar program comes from PixInsight's update system (package "Gaia Depth Grade sidecar"); the script downloads, unpacks and installs nothing. Working files and online Gaia query results live in a private per-user directory, ~/.cache/gaia-depth-grade (mode 0700, checked before use). Earlier versions used ~/.astro-pi/gaia-depth-grade, which you may delete.
